subject: Success signposts & gating tests for pilot wrap — ClearSea MAP
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.inference>
To: Parker Evans <parker@clearseahealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.inference>
Date: Fri, 25 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Draft MAP + candidate success signposts for the pilot

Parker — attaching a short Mutual Action Plan (MAP) draft focused on how we’ll evaluate success and the specific gating tests we propose for the pilot. High-level items in this version:

- Success signposts (what "good" looks like): latency, format fidelity, token-cost per session, and downstream accuracy for core workflows.
- Exit gates / Go/no-go checkpoints at 2 weeks and 4 weeks.
- Acceptance tests: smoke-load, format-conformance, and 50-case human evaluation for correctness.

Quick ask: can you confirm a preferred cutover window (week of Aug 11 or Aug 18) and whether procurement needs the MAP as a PDF or a short SOW? I’ve attached ClearSea_MAP_v0.9.pdf and a CSV with proposed smoke tests.

Next steps I suggest: internal dev run of smoke tests (owner: Karthik), a short customer review call, and a brief pilot canary (2% traffic) for the first 24 hours after cutover.

- Soojin

Attachments:
- ClearSea_MAP_v0.9.pdf (pdf)
- smoke-test-cases.csv (csv)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.inference>, Parker Evans <parker@clearseahealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.inference>
Date: Sat, 26 Jul 2025 16:04:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Draft MAP + candidate success signposts for the pilot

Thanks — reviewed the MAP. A few technical acceptance tests we should lock in (short list):

- Latency: end-to-end p95 < 350ms for 512-token average queries under expected pilot load (target test: 1000 x production-like queries).
- Throughput/Autoscale: 99th percentile of request success under a 3x burst for 10 minutes with no dropped requests.
- Response schema and function-calling: 100% of sampled responses must pass schema validation for the 12 documented endpoints.
- Embedding stability: mean cosine similarity within 0.02 of baseline for 200 sample vectors.
- Safety and hallucination check: <5% critical hallucination rate on the 50-case human-eval suite; any failures trigger rollback.

I annotated the MAP PDF with suggested thresholds and added the smoke-test-cases.csv rows for the p95 load profile. If ClearSea wants to relax the latency threshold for the first week, we can flag the canary as a rolling pass/fail rather than a hard gate.

Karthik

---
On Sat, 26 Jul 2025 at 09:12 Soojin Lee wrote:
> Parker — attaching a short Mutual Action Plan (MAP) draft focused on how we’ll evaluate success and the specific gating tests we propose for the pilot.

From: Parker Evans <parker@clearseahealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.inference>
Cc: ClearSea Health Procurement <procurement@clearseahealth.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>
Date: Sun, 27 Jul 2025 13:30:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Draft MAP + candidate success signposts for the pilot

Soojin / Karthik — thanks for the draft and the clear thresholds. A few quick items from our side:

- Procurement prefers a PDF MAP that we can attach to our internal approval packet. The PDF you sent is good; if you can add a one-page SOW snippet we’ll be able to fast-track.
- Timeline: ClearSea prefers the Aug 18 cutover window (one extra week to align schedules).
- Evaluation scope: we can run the 50-case human evaluation internally but need the sample prompt bank + scoring rubric (format/concordance vs. clinical accuracy). Can you hand off the rubric?
- Risk tolerance: we can accept a temporary latency relaxation to p95 < 420ms during a 48-hour ramp as long as functionality thresholds (schema validation and hallucination guardrail) are strict.

Also — small ask on attachments: can you include a CSV with the 50 human-eval cases and a canonical scoring column? That makes our QA signoff much faster.

Parker

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.inference>
To: Parker Evans <parker@clearseahealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 28 Jul 2025 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft MAP + candidate success signposts for the pilot — agreed items and owners

Great — thanks Parker. Recap and confirmed actions below (short and actionable):

1) Timeline
- Agreed cutover window: week of Aug 18.
- Canary plan: 2% traffic for first 24h, rolling to 10% over 48h if canary passes.

2) Success signposts / Acceptance tests (finalized):
- Latency: target p95 < 350ms; temporary allowance p95 < 420ms during 48h ramp only.
- Schema conformance: 100% pass on sampled responses for the 12 endpoints.
- Human-eval: 50-case bank, pass threshold: >= 85% format+correctness score; any critical failure triggers immediate rollback.
- Embedding drift: mean cosine delta <= 0.02 on 200 vectors.
- Reliability: no more than 1% error rate under 3x burst test.

3) Deliverables (owners & due dates)
- MAP + one-paragraph SOW (Soojin) — PDF by Tue Jul 29 EOD.
- 50-case human-eval CSV + rubric (Marcus) — Wed Jul 30 EOD.
- Internal smoke-run and p95 load run (Karthik) — run by Thu Jul 31; results posted to the MAP doc.

4) Docs and approvals
- I’ll attach the finalized PDF to HubSpot and share the Google Doc link. Procurement will get the SOW snippet; Parker, please confirm any special clause language you need.

If that mapping looks right I’ll finalize the MAP PDF and send the formal SOW blurb for procurement. Small ask for procurement: confirm whether they need a separate technical appendix or if an embedded appendix in the MAP PDF is fine.

Thanks — Soojin

Attachments referenced:
- ClearSea_MAP_v0.9.pdf (will update with SOW)
- smoke-test-cases.csv
